members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same timeout-arming code in protocol.ts's request timeout handling (base commit 637be389aa) to fix how the pending timer is (re)armed with respect to maxTotalTimeout when progress notifications reset the per-request timeout. #2763's changeset explicitly states the fix covers both the initial arm ('whichever limit comes first') and the progress-reset case ('progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget'), which is the exact same code path #2817 touches (the block that does clearTimeout(info.timeoutId); ...; info.timeoutId = setTimeout(...) on a progress notification). (2 PRs)
members.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same timeout-arming code in protocol.ts's request timeout handling (base commit 637be389aa) to fix how the pending timer is (re)armed with respect to maxTotalTimeout when progress notifications reset the per-request timeout. #2763's changeset explicitly states the fix covers both the initial arm ('whichever limit comes first') and the progress-reset case ('progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget'), which is the exact same code path #2817 touches (the block that does clearTimeout(info.timeoutId); ...; info.timeoutId = setTimeout(...) on a progress notification). members.cluster_pick_reason: 2763 ships a changeset file bumping @modelcontextprotocol/core-internal, client, and server (required for release), while 2817 has no changeset at all. 2763's fix changes the actual delay computation (Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout)) so the cap is enforced both on initial arm and on progress-driven resets. 2817 only adds info.startTime = Date.now() and continues to re-arm with the full info.timeout on each progress reset, so it does not change the delay used and would not by itself stop maxTotalTimeout from being exceeded after a progress notification — its own diff shows only a test comment update, not a new/updated assertion proving the cap is enforced.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2600: Both fix the same bug: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves in-flight JSON-response-mode POST requests hanging forever instead of settling their pending Promise<Response>, because cleanup only tears down stream mappings without resolving the parked response.

clusters.pick_reason: 2763 ships a changeset file bumping @modelcontextprotocol/core-internal, client, and server (required for release), while 2817 has no changeset at all. 2763's fix changes the actual delay computation (Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout)) so the cap is enforced both on initial arm and on progress-driven resets. 2817 only adds info.startTime = Date.now() and continues to re-arm with the full info.timeout on each progress reset, so it does not change the delay used and would not by itself stop maxTotalTimeout from being exceeded after a progress notification — its own diff shows only a test comment update, not a new/updated assertion proving the cap is enforced.

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same timeout-arming code in protocol.ts's request timeout handling (base commit 637be389aa) to fix how the pending timer is (re)armed with respect to maxTotalTimeout when progress notifications reset the per-request timeout. #2763's changeset explicitly states the fix covers both the initial arm ('whichever limit comes first') and the progress-reset case ('progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget'), which is the exact same code path #2817 touches (the block that does clearTimeout(info.timeoutId); ...; info.timeoutId = setTimeout(...) on a progress notification). (2 PRs)
